subject: Career
title: Negotiating Equity and Stock Options
description: A short lesson to help you apply Negotiating Equity and Stock Options.

hook.text: They offer 10,000 stock options. Sounds exciting until you learn the strike price, vesting, and dilution.

buildup.text: Options give you the right to buy shares at a set price. They're worthless if the company doesn't grow.

discovery.text: Key questions: what's the current valuation, total shares outstanding, and vesting schedule?

twist.text: 10,000 options out of 100 million shares is 0.01%. The number means nothing without context.

climax.text: At startups, negotiate for a percentage, not a number. Percentages resist dilution better.

punchline.text: Options are a bet. Understand the odds first.

quiz.question: What makes stock option grants meaningful?
options: The percentage of total shares, not just the number

details.summary: Equity negotiation requires understanding option types, vesting schedules, strike prices, and dilution risk. Stock options and restricted stock units differ fundamentally in tax treatment and liquidity, making informed negotiation essential for maximizing value.
details.whyItMatters: Equity can represent the most valuable part of a compensation package, especially at high-growth companies. Misunderstanding its terms can mean leaving substantial wealth on the table.
takeaways: ISOs and RSUs have very different tax and liquidity profiles
Always negotiate vesting acceleration in addition to grant size
Factor dilution expectations into your equity valuation

faq.question: What is the difference between ISOs and RSUs in practical terms?
faq.answer: Incentive Stock Options give you the right to buy shares at a set price and may qualify for favorable capital gains tax treatment. RSUs are granted shares that vest over time and are taxed as ordinary income upon vesting. RSUs have no purchase cost.

faq.question: How should I evaluate equity at a pre-IPO startup?
faq.answer: Request the latest 409A valuation, total fully diluted share count, and any anticipated funding rounds. Calculate your percentage ownership and apply a discount for illiquidity and execution risk. Compare the expected outcome to guaranteed cash.
